answer: Proposed archive rule: one daily listing per ID requires a distinct 1 GiB proof-of-replication encoding to mirror sonnet texts and juniper genomes. Validators check ID-bound setup proofs and random timed reads throughout the day; failure revokes the listing. Sampling can miss deletion; the bound assumes regeneration exceeds the response deadline. Disks are reusable capital; power recurs; no stake is locked. Pooling and parallelism can lower unit costs, not reuse replicas: ten IDs need 10 GiB concurrently under that assumption.
